situation.note: i don't want to be here anymore. i've been thinking about how to end it. nothing matters.

understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call not feeling good enough, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.week_thesis: By the end of the week the thought that nothing matters is named, and the part of you that asks is held as real and not ending.

week_beats.hook: You recognise the weight of the thought and the numbness, named without judgment.
week_beats.diagnose: You see that it is a state of mind, not the truth of who you are.
week_beats.steady: You hold that the self that asks is not the self that ends.
week_beats.act: You try one act of staying with someone you trust and not acting on the thought.
week_beats.story: A young seeker who felt the world was empty shows you that what is real in you cannot end.

understanding.core_struggle: A student under twenty-five says they do not want to be here anymore and thinks about ending it, finding nothing meaningful.
understanding.mirror: It sounds like you're carrying something very heavy right now.
understanding.insight: What you're carrying is heavy, and it is not a measure of your worth. You don't have to carry it alone.

queries.hook: When the darkness feels endless and the heart is too tired to go on, and no one seems to see the pain.
queries.diagnose: When the mind turns against itself, it says nothing matters and that life should end; this is a state of mind, not the truth of who you are.
queries.steady: This darkness is a passing night, not the whole of you; the self within you is whole, held and never alone.
queries.act: Hold on through the dark night and reach out to someone who cares; the self within you is not broken and is never alone.
queries.story: A young seeker who felt the world was empty and the self was small, who found the truth that is not born and does not die.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the inner happiness of one who sees clearly.
verse.sanskrit: योऽन्तःसुखोऽन्तरारामस्तथान्तर्ज्योतिरेव यः । स योगी ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं ब्रह्मभूतोऽधिगच्छति ॥
verse.line: Happy within, at ease within, lit from within: that person finds lasting freedom.
verse.translation: One whose happiness is within, whose delight is within, and whose light is within, that yogi becomes one with Brahman and reaches the peace of Brahman.

words.en: becoming one with the supreme reality

verse.why: Pleasures that start and end can't hold your happiness; find the joy within.

matched.label: Nothing is wrong but nothing feels meaningful

prasang.title: The yoga of knowledge
prasang.summary: Krishna describes the wise: equal-eyed towards all beings, not elated or crushed, finding joy within, seeing that sense pleasures end in sorrow, and able to withstand desire and anger.
prasang.lesson: Pleasures that start and end can't hold your happiness; find the joy within.

verse.meaning: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna on the battlefield. The war has not yet begun, and Arjuna is paralyzed by grief and confusion. Krishna is describing the person who has found inner light. This person is not happy because of what they own or achieve. Their happiness is not dependent on the world outside them. It comes from inside. Krishna says this inner light is steady. It does not flicker with praise or criticism. It is not created by success or destroyed by failure. This person has seen that pleasure from outside things always ends.
verse.for_you: You are sitting with your phone and the thought that nothing matters. That is a heavy thing to carry. The verse does not tell you to fix that feeling right now. It simply names a different kind of light.
verse.try_today: Notice one small thing that is not on your screen, and let it rest in your mind for a moment.
verse.scene_line: You are on the edge of a battlefield, and your own light is waiting to be named.

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Ashma (quoted by Vyasa)
verse.setting: The sage Ashma answers King Janaka, who asks how to stay steady when people and wealth come and go.
verse.sanskrit: मानसानां पुनर्योनिर्दुःखानां चित्तविभ्रमः / अनिष्टोपनिपातो वा तृतीयं नोपपद्यते
verse.line: Mental pain comes from two places: something you didn't want happened, or your mind is spinning. No third.
verse.translation: Sorrow of the mind has only two sources: a confused, wandering mind, or something unwanted happening to you. There is no third.
verse.why: Days don't come back. Grieve, then steady yourself with the people still in front of you.

prasang.title: Ashma Gita: the sage on bearing loss
prasang.summary: Vyasa tells the grieving Yudhishthira how the sage Ashma consoled King Janaka: pain comes from what we didn't want or what we lost; meetings end; days don't return; ask who you are and steady the mind.
prasang.lesson: Days don't come back. Grieve, then steady yourself with the people still in front of you.

verse.for_you: A mistake is something you did, not who you are; no one who tries to do good is ever lost.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.setting: Closing verse of the section on steadfastness.
verse.sanskrit: छिन्नोऽपि रोहति तरुश्चन्द्रः क्षीणोऽपि वर्धते लोके । इति विमृशन्तः सन्तः सन्तप्यन्ते न लोकेऽस्मिन् ॥
verse.line: A cut tree grows back; the waning moon fills again. Remembering this, the wise do not despair.
verse.translation: A tree that is cut grows again; the waning moon waxes again in the world. Reflecting on this, the good are not tormented in this world.
verse.why: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On steadfastness
prasang.summary: Steadfastness: the gods kept churning the ocean past jewels and poison until they found nectar; the steady do not leave the right path whatever people say. A struck ball bounces back and a cut tree grows again.
prasang.lesson: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

verse.for_you: You are sitting in the quiet after the storm, and the numbness is heavy. But this numbness is not the end. It is a season, not the whole year. The part of you that is asking, that is still here and still breathing, is the part that will grow back.
verse.try_today: Notice one small thing that returns to normal today.

verse.speaker: Ashtavakra
verse.setting: King Janaka asks the young sage Ashtavakra how a person becomes free.
verse.sanskrit: त्वया व्याप्तमिदं विश्वं त्वयि प्रोतं यथार्थतः । शुद्धबुद्धस्वरूपस्त्वं मा गमः क्षुद्रचित्तताम् ॥
verse.line: You are pure awareness, wider than any worry. Don't let your mind shrink into pettiness.
verse.translation: This whole universe is pervaded by you and strung on you. By nature you are pure awareness; do not fall into smallness of mind.
verse.why: You are more than your roles and worries; freedom starts with how you see yourself.

prasang.title: Janaka asks the boy-sage how to be free
prasang.summary: King Janaka, ruler of Mithila, asks the young sage Ashtavakra three questions: how to gain wisdom, freedom and dispassion. Ashtavakra answers at once: you are not the body or your roles but the awareness that watches them, and freedom is available now.
prasang.story_hook: A powerful king bowed before a boy whose body was bent in eight places, and asked him how to be free.
prasang.lesson: You are more than your roles and worries; freedom starts with how you see yourself.

verse.meaning: King Janaka sits with the young sage Ashtavakra, asking how a person finds freedom. Ashtavakra looks at him and says the whole universe is strung on you. You are not the roles you play or the worries you carry. You are the awareness that watches them. Freedom is not something you gain. It is what you are already, wider than any thought of not being enough.
verse.for_you: You are sitting with your phone, feeling empty. The voice that says you do not want to be here anymore is a thought, not the whole of you. You are the awareness that notices the emptiness. That noticing is real and it is not ending.
verse.try_today: Notice the part of you that sees the emptiness without becoming it.
verse.scene_line: You are the awareness that watches the empty screen.

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: Vasishtha on the fourth gatekeeper: good company (satsanga).
verse.sanskrit: अपि कष्टतरां प्राप्तैर्दशां विवशतां गतैः । मनागपि न संत्याज्या मानवैः साधुसंगतिः ॥
verse.line: Even at your lowest and most helpless, don't let go of good company.
verse.translation: Even when people fall into the hardest straits and feel helpless, they should not let go of good company, not even a little.
verse.why: Pick one of calm, clear thinking, contentment or good company. Grow it, and the others follow.

prasang.title: The four gatekeepers: calm, inquiry, contentment, good company
prasang.summary: Vasishtha tells Rama that four gatekeepers guard the door to freedom: calm, inquiry, contentment and good company. He gives a chapter to each, then says you only need to start with one, because each one strengthens the others.
prasang.lesson: Pick one of calm, clear thinking, contentment or good company. Grow it, and the others follow.

verse.meaning: Vasishtha is telling Rama about the four gatekeepers that guard the door to freedom: calm, inquiry, contentment, and good company. He says you only need to start with one, because each one strengthens the others. He tells Rama that even when people fall into the hardest straits and feel helpless, they should not let go of good company, not even a little.
verse.for_you: The texts say that even in the deepest helplessness, good company is a gatekeeper to freedom. You do not have to carry this alone.
verse.try_today: Reach out to one person you trust and just stay with them.
verse.scene_line: You are at the gate, and good company is the key.

verse.speaker: Dharmavyadha (the righteous meat-seller)
verse.setting: In Mithila, a meat-seller famed for wisdom teaches a proud ascetic what goodness really is.
verse.sanskrit: पापं चेत्पुरुषः कृत्वा कल्याणमभिपद्यते / मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्यो महाभ्रेणेव चन्द्रमाः
verse.line: Turn to doing good after a wrong, and you come out like the moon from behind a cloud.
verse.translation: If a person who has done wrong turns to doing good, he is freed from all his wrongs, like the moon coming out from behind a great cloud.
verse.why: Wisdom lives in ordinary people doing ordinary work honestly. Care for your parents.

prasang.title: Vyadha Gita: the butcher who taught a sage
prasang.summary: A proud ascetic, Kaushika, is sent to learn from a meat-seller in Mithila. The butcher teaches him plain goodness: don't return evil, repent and resolve, keep envy away, care for your parents, and don't spend your one life making enemies.
prasang.lesson: Wisdom lives in ordinary people doing ordinary work honestly. Care for your parents.

verse.for_you: Be on your own side: lift yourself up, make amends where you can, and begin again; no one who does good is lost.

story.title: Rama comes home from his pilgrimage and loses interest in everything
story.story_hook: The prince who had everything came back from his travels and stopped laughing.
story.summary: Sixteen-year-old Rama returns from a long pilgrimage and quietly withdraws: he stops eating properly, stops laughing, ignores his duties and sits alone. His attendants tell the worried king. Vishvamitra and Vasishtha say this is not illness or weakness but the first stirring of real questions, and ask that Rama be brought to them.
story.lesson: Losing interest in everything can be the start of asking better questions, if someone helps you through it.

anchor.speaker: Rama's attendant
anchor.setting: Rama's attendants tell King Dasharatha how the prince has changed since his pilgrimage.
anchor.sanskrit: रामो राजीवपत्राक्षो यतःप्रभृति चागतः । सविप्रस्तीर्थयात्रायास्ततःप्रभृति दुर्मनाः ॥
anchor.line: Ever since he came back from the trip, he hasn't been himself.
anchor.translation: Ever since lotus-eyed Rama came back from his pilgrimage with the brahmins, he has been low in spirit.
anchor.why: Losing interest in everything can be the start of asking better questions, if someone helps you through it.
